title: Senior Counsel (Commercial Contracts & Partnerships)
description:
Department: Legal

Location: Remote, U.S.

Employment Type: Full-time

Reports To: Chief Legal Officer

About Midi Health

At Midi Health, we are redefining healthcare for women in midlife. Our virtual care model connects patients with specialized clinicians and personalized care plans, making high-quality menopause and midlife healthcare accessible across the country.

The Role

We are seeking a Senior Counsel (Commercial Contracts & Partnerships) to lead legal support across Midi’s commercial ecosystem. In this role, you will own a broad deal portfolio—including payor, strategic partnership, enterprise commercial, vendor, marketing, and influencer agreements. We are looking for a practical, business-minded deal lawyer who can effectively manage risk, drive revenue velocity, and build scalable contracting processes as Midi expands nationwide.

Reporting directly to the Chief Legal Officer, you will serve as a key legal partner to business leaders across Commercial, Payor, Marketing, Finance, Clinical, Product, and Operations.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Contracting

  • Draft, review, negotiate, and manage commercial agreements, including master services agreements, statements of work, order forms, amendments, renewals, business associate agreements, data processing agreements, and other transaction documents.

  • Advise internal stakeholders on contract structure, risk allocation, approvals, escalation points, and implementation requirements.

  • Maintain and improve contract templates, clause libraries, fallback positions, playbooks, and approval workflows.

  • Review customer, partner, and vendor paper and identify issues involving indemnification, limitation of liability, insurance, intellectual property, confidentiality, data rights, audit rights, termination, publicity, and regulatory compliance.

  • Support high-volume contracting while escalating material, novel, or strategically significant issues to the Chief Legal Officer.

Payor & Healthcare Partnerships

  • Support agreements with health plans, employers, benefits consultants, brokers, third-party administrators, healthcare platforms, and other strategic partners.

  • Draft and negotiate payor and partnership agreements involving referrals, patient access, care delivery, implementation, reporting, fees, performance standards, clinical services, marketing, and data sharing.

  • Partner with Commercial and Strategic Alliances teams from initial opportunity through negotiation, signature, implementation, renewal, and termination.

  • Advise on healthcare contracting issues involving fee structures, patient choice, clinical independence, licensure, privacy, business associate obligations, quality measures, service levels, and regulatory risk.

  • Help create repeatable contracting frameworks for Midi’s growing partner ecosystem.

Vendor & Procurement Agreements

  • Review and negotiate vendor agreements, SaaS agreements, professional services agreements, technology agreements, marketing agreements, and operational contracts.

  • Assess vendor risk based on data access, clinical impact, patient-facing activity, operational criticality, contract value, and security posture.

  • Coordinate with Procurement, Finance, Information Security, Privacy, Product, and Operations on vendor intake, diligence, approvals, renewals, and offboarding.

  • Support vendor notices, amendments, termination letters, transition documentation, and contract rationalization.

  • Improve vendor contracting standards, templates, workflows, and reporting.

Influencer, Marketing & Consumer Agreements

  • Draft and negotiate influencer, creator, affiliate, sponsorship, ambassador, media, and marketing agreements.

  • Advise Marketing and Brand teams on disclosures, endorsements, testimonials, health claims, advertising substantiation, intellectual property, usage rights, exclusivity, approvals, and content takedown rights.

  • Support consumer-facing initiatives involving Midi’s store, supplements, compounded cosmetics, patient education, social media, and digital campaigns.

  • Coordinate with regulatory and privacy counsel on claims, consumer data, patient stories, testimonials, and health-related marketing content.

Contract Management & Legal Operations

  • Maintain contract repositories, matter trackers, renewal calendars, obligation trackers, and reporting processes.

  • Help implement and improve Midi’s contract lifecycle management system, including intake, templates, approval routing, signature, storage, renewals, and post-signature obligations.

  • Develop practical guidance that enables business teams to use approved templates and resolve routine contract questions efficiently.

  • Identify recurring negotiation issues and convert them into playbooks, standard language, and self-service resources.

  • Use legal technology and artificial intelligence tools responsibly to improve contract review, drafting, issue spotting, and knowledge management.

Cross-Functional Legal Advice

  • Serve as a trusted legal advisor to Commercial, Strategic Alliances, Payor, Finance, Procurement, Marketing, Clinical, Product, Privacy, Information Security, and Executive Leadership teams.

  • Explain contract terms and legal risk in clear business language.

  • Balance speed, revenue objectives, patient impact, and risk management when recommending deal structures and negotiation positions.

  • Coordinate with outside counsel on specialized commercial, healthcare, privacy, intellectual property, and regulatory matters.

What We’re Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Education & Bar Admission: J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar (California bar preferred).
  • Experience: 8+ years of practicing legal experience with substantial time focused on drafting and negotiating commercial agreements.
  • Healthcare Domain Depth: Meaningful healthcare legal experience advising a healthcare provider, digital health company, telehealth business, health plan, healthcare services company, or healthcare-focused law firm.
  • Practice Background: Experience working at a law firm and/or in-house legal department (ideally a mix of both).
  • Contracting Breadth: Substantial experience across at least three of the following: payor agreements, strategic partnerships, vendor agreements, SaaS agreements, professional services, marketing agreements, influencer agreements, DPAs, or BAAs.
  • Legal Tech & AI: Proficiency using legal technology and artificial intelligence tools responsibly to enhance efficiency and drafting precision.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in digital health, virtual care, women’s health, pharmacy, supplements, compounded products, or consumer healthcare.
  • Experience negotiating directly with health plans, enterprise employers, benefits consultants, brokers, or healthcare platforms.
  • Familiarity with FTC advertising and endorsement issues, health claims, patient testimonials, or influencer marketing.
  • Experience supporting HIPAA, state health privacy, information security, and healthcare data requirements within commercial transactions.
  • Hands-on experience implementing or administering CLM systems (e.g., Ironclad, Salesforce, DocuSign CLM) and building contract playbooks or clause libraries.

Key Competencies

  • Commercial Dealmaking & Judgment: Practical, business-oriented approach to risk with strong contract judgment and the ability to distinguish routine terms from material risk requiring escalation.
  • Prioritization & Speed: Ability to manage multiple high-velocity negotiations and diverse cross-functional stakeholders simultaneously without sacrificing attention to detail.
  • Clear Communication: Ability to translate complex legal terms and risks into clear, actionable business recommendations.
  • Adaptability & Collaboration: Comfortable operating with ambiguity, building processes in a high-growth environment, and working with humility, curiosity, and persistence.
  • Mission Alignment: Commitment to Midi’s mission of expanding access to high-quality healthcare for women in midlife.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Salary Range: $200,000 - $230,000 / year. Final compensation will be determined based on candidate experience, skills, location, qualifications, and internal equity.
  • Additional Comp: Eligible for equity and benefits.

Our Benefits Include:

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • New-hire home office equipment stipend + monthly remote work stipend
  • Dynamic, remote-first company culture

Why Join Midi Health?

Midlife women’s health has been neglected by traditional healthcare for far too long. At Midi, we are changing that by building the nation’s leading virtual care clinic dedicated to menopause and midlife care—one of the fastest-growing sectors in digital health.

As Senior Counsel, you won't just be reviewing contracts; you will be architecting the strategic partnerships, payor agreements, and commercial frameworks that allow us to scale nationwide. You’ll join a collaborative, high-velocity legal team where your business judgment is trusted, your work directly drives revenue, and your impact is felt by thousands of women receiving life-changing care every single day.

title: Wastewater Operator
description:
Woodard & Curran is a national engineering, science and operations firm with a simple vision for clean water, a safe environment, healthy communities and happy people. As an employee-owned company, we strive to cultivate teams that encourage collaboration in an inclusive culture. We seek talented individuals from all backgrounds to help us address a broad range of water and environmental issues. We prioritize our people, offering opportunities for professional growth, ownership and flexibility. This commitment enables us to make a meaningful impact on our clients, communities and the planet.


Woodard & Curran draws on the experience of hundreds of certified operators across the country, backed by the knowledge and skills of hundreds more engineers, scientists, and regulatory experts, to quickly tackle the most challenging operational issues and keep treatment plants running efficiently and in full compliance. Woodard & Curran also reimburse employees in earning, upgrading, and keeping their licenses and certifications within the industry.
​
The Wastewater Operator regularly participates in the daily operations and maintenance of 2 Wastewater Treatment Facilities as directed by the Project Manager and Chief Operator. If you enjoy working outdoors protecting nature’s precious resource, water, then you will find this position challenging and rewarding. This position comes with the opportunity for upward mobility to advance your career in the utility field. Woodard & Curran is dedicated to our employees’ growth and development and wants to help you on your career path!
Schedule:
Tuesday – Saturday, or Sunday - Thursday, 7:00am-3:00pm pm. Flexibility and extended shifts to meet the seasonal demands of the wastewater system. Reliable and dependable attendance is an essential function of the position. Availability for standby duty and the ability to be “on-call,” working evenings, weekends and holidays as needed. Response to emergency events and alarm call-outs required as scheduled and required.
- On-call, incentives offer $200 for the week you are on call (this is on a rotation).
- Compensation for being on call is 2hrs minimum paid for each call out received.

  • Monitor wastewater treatment plant processes and equipment both manually and via SCADA automation, adjusting as necessary to control their operation.
  • Perform water quality sampling, testing, and analysis to determine compliance with federal, state, and EPA standards.
  • Operate, maintain, control, and perform routine repair of plant equipment, including preventive maintenance duties.

  • Recognize deviations or irregularities in the plant operation and maintenance; adjust the plant process and equipment in order to maintain the required quality standards of the federal, state, and county regulatory agencies.
  • Sample, measure, and test plant values such as pH, chlorine residuals, temperature, levels, and others; make corrections and adjustments; collect required samples for on and offsite analysis.
  • Collaborate with maintenance staff on specific projects; adjust or bypass job specific areas, processes, or equipment to ensure consistent water production, plant integrity, and safety.
  • Test, monitor, record, evaluate, troubleshoot, and adjust the operation of plant emergency generator and auxiliary equipment.
  • Assist contractors and consultants with specific tasks.
  • Assist in preparing standard operating procedures.
  • Oversee Plant operations to remain in compliance of all Federal, State, County and City regulations and standards.
  • Ensure compliance with safety regulations and standard operating procedures.
  • Work around high voltage, rotating equipment and various hazardous chemicals.
  • Performs related work as required.

title: Executive Advisor- Water Economics & Infrastructure Investment Strategy
description:
To solve complex challenges, you need to challenge the status-quo.

At GHD Advisory we are invested in creating sustainable commercial outcomes with clients driving change in water, energy and urbanization.

Join a team committed to solving complex challenges across the value chain, from capital deployment to asset management, enabling resilience, growth and sustainability.

Together, we’ll help create a future for generations to come.

Who are we looking for?

GHD Advisory is seeking an Executive Advisor – Water Economics & Infrastructure Investment Strategy to lead and grow our water sector financial advisory and investment facilitation capabilities from the NYC Metro Area. This is a senior, client-facing leadership role for someone who operates at the intersection of water utility management, infrastructure economics, and private capital mobilization.

You will serve as a trusted intermediary between municipal water and wastewater clients and private sector investors, helping utilities unlock new funding pathways, structure innovative financing, and deliver infrastructure more effectively. You will bring deep knowledge of U.S. municipal finance alongside a working understanding of international alternative delivery and investment models — including P3/PPP frameworks used in Australia, the UK, Canada, and Asia-Pacific — and help translate those approaches for the U.S. market.

This role will be central to GHD's strategy to build a nationally recognized Water Economics and Investment Advisory practice within our Asset Management group, backed by our global platform and track record across 61+ P3 projects worldwide.

This individual will act as a strategic financial and investment advisor to water and wastewater utilities, helping clients optimize capital investment, funding strategies, and infrastructure delivery. The position combines expertise in infrastructure finance, public-private partnerships (P3s), and alternative delivery models to develop innovative funding solutions, facilitate private sector investment, and guide complex procurement strategies. As a trusted advisor to utility executives, the role also leads business development, mentors multidisciplinary teams, and brings global best practices to deliver integrated, financially sustainable infrastructure solutions.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

  • Business Development & Market Growth
    • Assist expansion and mining of existing on-call contracts with municipal/regional water clients.
    • Shape and win water AM task orders under newly awarded on-calls and future pursuits.
    • Conduct market positioning, client outreach, opportunity qualification, and pursuit leadership.
    • Lead proposal development, interview preparation, scope development, and pricing strategies.
    • Build and maintain relationships with regulatory agencies, municipal utilities, private water companies, and partner firms.
  • Project Delivery & Technical Responsibilities
    • Serve as Project Manager or Technical Lead on water AM and economic advisory projects, including:
      • Asset management plans & maturity assessments
      • Risk-based capital planning and prioritization
      • Lifecycle costing and long-term financial modeling
      • Investment strategies and rate/fee impacts
      • Business case development using economic, financial, and risk frameworks
      • AM program governance, policy, and organizational design
      • Digital AM enablement (CMMS, EAM, GIS, analytics)
      • Program management and owner advisor delivery
    • Integrate engineering, economics, finance, and asset performance insights.
    • Manage multidisciplinary teams across advisory, engineering, and digital groups.
  • Client Engagement & Leadership
    • Engage utility executives and senior decision-makers to provide trusted advisory insights.
    • Mentor early-career AM professionals in financial modeling, risk frameworks, and program strategy.
    • Contribute to development of GHD AM tools, methodologies, and sector strategies.
  • Consulting Project/Program Design: Design the project architecture, building on the initial proposal and the client interviews to develop a solution that meets the client's stated requirements and addresses any identified client issues.
  • Client Issue Diagnosis: Collate and conduct analysis of the tactical and operational information gathered through interviews and research to support the diagnosis of underlying client issues and problems and the design of single solutions.
  • Client Issue Clarification: Conduct interviews following an established framework of questions to gather information on client issues.
  • Personal Capability Building: Act as subject matter expert in an area of technology, policy, regulation, or operational management for the team. Maintain external accreditations and in-depth understanding of current and emerging external regulation and industry best practices through continuing professional development, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
  • Business Advice: Lead a highly complex business advisory process, ensuring alignment with the organization's strategic initiatives and goals.

What you’ll bring to the team:

  • 20+ years of experience in infrastructure finance, water/wastewater utility economics, investment advisory, or related fields
  • Professional Engineer (PE) or equivalent professional credential (CFA, PFM, or comparable financial certification also valued)
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Economics, Finance, Public Policy, or related field
  • Deep expertise in water and wastewater utility operations and finance — including rate structures, capital planning, CIP development, and regulatory frameworks
  • Proven experience structuring or facilitating P3/PPP transactions, alternative delivery, or private capital placement for municipal infrastructure
  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. municipal finance instruments — municipal bonds, SRF, WIFIA, environmental impact bonds, credit facilities
  • Familiarity with international alternative delivery and financing models (e.g., Australian alliance contracting, UK DPC, Asian infrastructure investment models)
  • Demonstrated ability to engage and advise C-suite utility executives and municipal finance leaders (GMs, CFOs, finance directors, elected officials)
  • Experience working with or alongside private investors, infrastructure funds, investment banks, or development finance institutions
  • Strong understanding of asset management principles — lifecycle planning, risk-based investment prioritization, capital optimization — and their connection to financial strategy
  • Exceptional communication skills — able to translate complex financial and technical concepts into clear, executive-ready recommendations
  • A relationship builder with a strong network in the water/wastewater utility and infrastructure finance community

title: Dozer Operator
description:
Overview

Posillico is Building for Generations.

Posillico is a multi-disciplined and diversified construction company. Along with our Civil /foundation group, Posillico’s business units include Wastewater Division, Environmental Division, Utilities Division, Drilling Division, Paving Division, Posillico Consulting LLC, Posillico Developmental LLC, and Posillico Materials, LLC. These companies give Posillico the unequalled, leveraged experience required to complete complex structural and geotechnical projects successfully.

Posillico empowers a “people first, think safety” culture throughout our organization. This “people first” culture has helped to promote and maintain an excellent record of accomplishment. Posillico has an exceptional safety program coupled with proactive employees throughout its management and union staff. We offer all employees an excellent opportunity to be part of our developing business at Posillico, as we set the standards for excellence in the construction industry with our integrated solutions.

Our company mission is to complete all our projects safely, on time, on target and on budget while having a positive impact in the community.

Follow us at… Facebook Instagram LinkedIn

Responsibilities

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Dozer Operator is responsible for safely and efficiently operating bulldozers and related heavy equipment used in site development, road construction, grading, and earthmoving projects. The ideal candidate has experience operating heavy machinery and can perform precision grading and material movement in a fast-paced outdoor construction environment while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and productivity.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Safely operate bulldozers in support of construction, grading, and earthmoving activities.
  • Perform rough and finish grading, land clearing, backfilling, spreading material, slope shaping, and site preparation.
  • Push, level, and distribute soil, rock, aggregate, and other construction materials according to project specifications.
  • Assist with road construction, pad preparation, embankment construction, erosion control, and utility backfill operations.
  • Read and interpret blueprints, grade stakes, site plans, and GPS machine control systems to ensure accurate grading.
  • Conduct daily pre- and post-operation inspections of equipment and report maintenance or safety concerns promptly.
  • Perform routine equipment maintenance, including checking fluid levels, greasing components, and cleaning equipment.
  • Work closely with supervisors, foremen, pipe crews, laborers, and other equipment operators to complete projects efficiently.
  • Maintain constant awareness of surroundings to avoid damage to underground utilities, structures, or personnel.
  • Operate equipment safely on varying terrain, including slopes and uneven ground.
  • Assist with manual labor and general site duties when equipment operation is not required.
  • Ensure compliance with all safety procedures, traffic control regulations, and equipment operating standards
  • Clean and maintain tools and equipment at the end of each shift
  • Perform other duties as assigned by supervisors.

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Minimum OSHA 10 certification required.
  • 2-5 years of experience operating bulldozers in heavy civil, road construction, grading, or site development projects preferred.
  • Valid driver's license required; CDL and equipment certifications preferred.
  • Ability to read construction plans, grade stakes, site layouts, and understand finish grade requirements.
  • Experience with GPS machine control systems (Topcon, Trimble, Leica, or similar) preferred.
  • Thorough knowledge of grading techniques, earthmoving operations, and soil compaction principles.
  • Understanding of equipment capabilities, limitations, and preventative maintenance requirements.
  • Ability to safely operate equipment on steep grades and in varying weather and site conditions.
  • Maintain a safe and secure work environment by complying with company policies, government standards, and legal regulations.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment, attention to detail, and strong safety awareness.
  • Ability to accurately judge distances, grades, elevations, and slopes.
  • Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, subcontractors, and survey personnel.
  • Follow instructions, meet production standards, and work independently with minimal supervision.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

Working Conditions:

Physical Demands:

  • Position requires physically demanding work in field conditions.
  • Must be able to stand, stoop, kneel, bend, crouch, and crawl for extended periods of time.
  • Possess physical strength to operate heavy and power-driven equipment.
  • Coordinate the use of eyes, hands, arms, and legs fully. Work easily and skillfully with hands.
  • Vision – ability to see details at close range and details at a distance (either naturally or with correction).
  • Lift up to 50 pounds, with frequent lifting and carrying of objects weighing up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to quickly and repeatedly adjust the controls of machines or vehicle to exact positions.
  • Ability to judge the distance between you and an object, depth perception.
  • Ability to respond to a signal when it appears, reaction time.

Environmental Conditions:

  • May work outside and exposed to weather.
  • Wear protective or safety equipment, i.e., safety boots/shoes, glasses, gloves, hearing protection, and hard hats.
  • May be exposed to high levels of noise, grease, dust, and a variety of substances that are typically associated with a construction site.
  • Work in dusty or dirty surroundings.

Location: Laredo, TX

title: Asset Protection Specialist (Part Time)
description:
The Role

At Green Thumb Industries and RISE Dispensaries, we believe the first impression is everything and that starts with you. As an Asset Protection Specialist (APS), you’re not just a security presence, you’re the warm, welcoming face of the dispensary and a key part of creating an elevated, friendly, concierge-style experience for our guests. This role is ideal for individuals who enjoy connecting with others, maintaining physical readiness to act with urgency, and ensuring everyone feels safe, respected, and cared for.

This is not your traditional security role. It’s a dynamic blend of hospitality, customer service, and safety leadership, designed to enhance both the customer journey and team member experience. Asset Protection Specialists are active, professional, and approachable stewards of our culture, safety, and brand values.

Key Responsibilities

Welcoming & Check-In Experience

  • Be the first smiling face our guests see—greet all visitors with warmth and positivity.
  • Manage check-in with professionalism and efficiency, while upholding compliance standards.
  • Set the “RISE Vibe” from the moment customers enter our doors.
  • Provide basic concierge-level support: answering common questions and directing traffic.

Safety, Security & Support

  • Serve as a visible, approachable, and responsive presence to deter incidents and ensure a sense of calm and order.
  • Monitor various areas of the premises, including the store entry/exit and site perimeters, to ensure safety, comfort, and compliance.
  • De-escalate situations with empathy, tact, and clear communication.
  • Support team members and store operations in matters of safety, cleanliness, compliance, and guest flow by escorting customers and visitors and remaining alert and mobile at all times.
  • Report and respond appropriately and urgently to any safety, security, or compliance incidents.
  • Support emergency procedures and preparedness, including fire, evacuation, or weather response.
  • Conduct visual inspections and checks per SOPs to maintain a secure and hazard-free environment.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Foster strong relationships and mutual trust with store teams, leadership, and customers.
  • Share insights on guest interactions, safety concerns, and security risks with transparency and discretion.
  • Support training of new APS team members to model warm, professional, and compliant behavior.
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • At least one year of customer-facing or concierge experience strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with POS systems and/or compliance technology preferred.
  • Security, military, or law enforcement experience is a plus when paired with a strong commitment to guest-first, hospitality-focused service.
  • Meet the scheduling and availability requirements (i.e., ability to work a schedule inclusive of varying shifts such as mornings, days, nights, and weekends) to meet business needs.
  • Must have reliable, responsible, and dependable attendance.
  • Must pass all required background checks including state-specific cannabis employment requirements.
  • Possess valid driver’s license or state ID.
  • Must be 21 years or older and meet all state-specific cannabis employment requirements.
  • Must be and remain compliant with all legal or company regulations for working in the cannabis industry.

Additional Requirements

Must have the ability to perform the following tasks for prolonged periods of time (i.e., up to the duration of a scheduled shift or workday)

  • Capable of remaining alert and responsive during extended periods of time.
  • Move about the dispensary to fulfill work assignments and assist patients and/or customers in various locations of the dispensary.
  • Remain in a stationary position, if required, to meet the needs of the business.
  • Converse and communicate with individuals and groups of people directly.
  • Operate point of sale system, computer, and other office productivity machinery to use online programming and software including word processing, database management, spreadsheet applications and email.
  • Inspect and receive detailed information, such as patients' and/or customers' dates of birth, order information, or inquiries.
  • Move inventory and materials weighing up to 30 pounds independently.
  • Position self to move inventory and materials in storage areas.
  • Comfortable standing or walking for extended periods, up to the duration of a scheduled shift or workday and working both indoors and outdoors.
  • Asset Protection Specialists are expected to maintain a visible and mobile presence throughout their shift. This is not a desk job—APS team members are regularly on their feet, engaging with guests, monitoring site activity, and supporting operations across the dispensary floor.

Skills

  • Friendly, professional demeanor with excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and empathetic in stressful situations.
  • Consistent demonstration of excellent customer service skills.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all employees.
  • Ability to listen well and effectively communicate, both verbally and in writing, with various audiences.
  • Understanding of applicable cannabis laws and regulations, safety regulations, local municipal codes and organizational rules, and standard operating procedures.
  • Employee must be able to follow instructions as directed and incorporate constructive criticism from managers.
  • Operate with a high level of professionalism and integrity, including dealing with confidential information and complying with HIPAA requirements.

Working Conditions

  • Engaging, fast-paced patient and customer-facing retail environment.
  • Outdoor duties in varying weather conditions may be required.
  • Exposure to cannabis and/or allergens that might be present in an environment where cannabis is present and prevalent.

We’re transparent—Honest and open communication keeps us healthy as an organization.
We’re collaborative—And believe good ideas can come from anywhere.
We have a growth mindset—One that’s grounded in well-being.

At GTI we believe that our corporate community should be a reflection of the communities we serve. We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity across race, sex, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, religion, experience, and thought—not only because it is right, but because it makes us better. GTI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

We can't wait to meet you.

title: Lead Software Engineer - Ai Engineer
description:

  • Design and develop creative full-stack software solutions using innovative approaches.

  • Drives team adoption of enterprise-authorized AI-assisted engineering practices within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and operational outcomes (e.g., AI-assisted code review/refactoring, test strategy acceleration, incident/root-cause analysis support), while establishing consistent validation standards (secure coding, peer review, automated testing) and promoting reuse of effective patterns across the team.

  • Applies knowledge of tools within the Software Development Life Cycle toolchain, including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development and automation capabilities, to improve the value realized by automation.
  • Architect and deliver cloud-native microservices and APIs (REST/streaming), ensuring scalability, resilience, and strong security controls.
  • Identify and automate solutions for recurring operational issues to improve system stability and observability (logs/metrics/tracing).
  • Communicate project status clearly and manage priorities across multiple initiatives.
  • Collaborate within a Scrum team, participate in Agile ceremonies, and support a culture of diversity, opportunity, and inclusion.
  • Codes in Java, AWS ECS, EKS, and Postgres
  • Utilizes AI agents (CoPilot, Claude) to improve quality and delivery timelines

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification in Software Engineering and 5+ years applied experience
  • Strong system design, application development, and operational stability skills in production environments.
  • Hands-on experience using enterprise-authorized AI-assisted software development tools within the work environment (e.g., for coding, test creation, troubleshooting, or documentation) with demonstrated ability to critically evaluate, validate, and refine AI-generated outputs for correctness, performance, and security.
  • Understanding of responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data sensitivity considerations, secure handling of inputs/outputs, and adherence to resiliency and security expectations; ability to guide peers on safe and effective usage within team practices.
  • Influence product design, application functionality, and technical operations within the team and domain by proposing pragmatic architectures, tradeoffs, and standards aligned to firm SDLC, security, and controls expectations.
  • Hands-on experience with Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI use cases (e.g., RAG, agents, prompt/tool orchestration, evaluation/guardrails).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML frameworks and ecosystems such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Hugging Face.
  • Experience with distributed systems and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
  • Expertise in microservices, RESTful APIs, and data technologies (relational and/or NoSQL).
  • Demonstrated experience leading effective use of approved AI-assisted software development tools (e.g., for coding, code review, test acceleration, troubleshooting) with the ability to set team expectations for validating AI outputs for correctness, performance, and security.
  • Practical experience building cloud-native systems (event-driven architectures, streaming, service mesh, etc.).

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

  • Cloud certification in AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Working knowledge of Python (for AI/ML integrations) a plus
  • Experience with multi region service deployments and zero downtime deployment
  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and modern CI/CD practices.
  • Strong understanding of responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data sensitivity considerations, secure handling of inputs/outputs
  • Strong communication skills and a proactive approach to continuous improvement.
  • Track record delivering scalable, reliable, and secure products from concept to launch.
  • Advanced Java proficiency (primary), plus working knowledge of Python (for AI/ML integrations) a plus.

description:

Drain Service Technician

Roto-Rooter operates businesses in over 100 company-owned branches, independent contractor territories, and approximately 400 independent franchise operations, serving approximately 90% of the U.S. population and parts of Canada.

If job security, top pay, excellent benefits, and career advancement representing a well-known national brand are what you are looking for, Roto-Rooter is the company for you. We pride ourselves on being a great place to work, providing excellent pay, flexible work schedules and top benefits.

title: Applied AI ML - Analyst

Implement and optimize Snowflake solutions (schemas, tables, views, micro-partitioning/clustering considerations, warehouse sizing, query tuning, data sharing patterns where applicable).
  • Understanding of data models for enterprise analytics (dimensional/star schemas, normalized models; applying standard banking data concepts where relevant). Create robust orchestration and scheduling (e.g., Airflow/MWAA, AWS Step Functions, etc.) with monitoring, alerting, retries, and operational runbooks.

Continuously evaluate and adopt emerging AI technologies to optimize ETL workflows, reduce manual effort, and enhance overall engineering productivity.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Bachelors degree in a quantitative or technical discipline or significant practical experience in industry.
  • Strong SQL skills (complex joins, window functions, query optimization, performance troubleshooting) and experience with AWS data services and cloud-native patterns (e.g., S3, IAM, KMS, Glue, Lambda, EMR, Step Functions, Kinesis/MSK—relevant mix).
  • Solid understanding of data modeling and how model choices impact performance, usability, and governance.
  • Practical experience with Snowflake (data loading, transformations, optimization, access controls). Proficiency in Python (or equivalent) for pipeline development, automation, and testing.
  • Experience with Git and CI/CD practices; familiarity with engineering standards for code reviews and automated testing.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Prior experience of developing solutions for Financial domain
  • Exposure to distributed model training, and deployment
  • Familiarity with techniques for model explainability and self-validation
  • Hands-on development experience with Spark (PySpark preferred) for large-scale processing.

title: Senior Buyer
description:
Senior Buyer

Position Summary

The Senior Buyer is responsible for managing purchasing activities in support of production schedules, customer requirements, inventory targets, and overall business needs. This role serves as a key point of ownership for supplier relationships and is responsible for placing, tracking, expediting, and managing purchase orders to ensure material availability, cost control, and supplier performance.

The Senior Buyer works closely with Program Management, Planning, Production, Engineering, Quality, Sales, and Finance to resolve material shortages, supplier issues, pricing concerns, account discrepancies, and delivery risks. This position requires strong judgment, independent decision-making, and the ability to manage complex purchasing situations in a fast-paced contract manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review and analyze material buy lists, MRP requirements, production schedules, and inventory needs to determine purchasing priorities.
  • Place, track, expedite, and reschedule purchase orders to support production requirements and customer commitments.
  • Coordinate purchasing activities with Program Management, Planning, Production, Engineering, Quality, Sales, and Finance.
  • Process purchase requisitions, purchase change orders, and requests for quote from approved suppliers.
  • Gather quotations, review bids, evaluate pricing, and make purchasing recommendations or awards.
  • Negotiate pricing, delivery, lead times, and other purchasing terms with suppliers.
  • Maintain inventory at planned levels using sound purchasing practices, including just-in-time purchasing and economic order quantity planning.
  • Monitor supplier performance related to cost, quality, delivery, responsiveness, and overall reliability.
  • Resolve receiving issues, supplier discrepancies, customer-related material issues, and AP/AR discrepancies in a timely and professional manner.
  • Work with suppliers to address shortages, late deliveries, nonconforming material, and other production-impacting issues.
  • Ensure material standards are met and that nonconformances, substitutions, or variances are properly reviewed and approved.
  • Perform cost analysis, volume planning, and sourcing reviews for assigned commodities, components, equipment, and services.
  • Identify and recommend cost-saving opportunities, alternate sourcing options, and make-versus-buy recommendations.
  • Evaluate supplier competitiveness and develop new supply sources when needed.
  • Support quote table maintenance, supplier database accuracy, part parameter updates, error report analysis, and supplier/part number information.
  • Monitor assigned subcontractors and suppliers to ensure performance meets cost, schedule, quality, and scope requirements.
  • Assist Sales, Program Management, and leadership with pricing support and contract negotiations as needed.
  • Provide accurate, prompt, professional, and courteous service to internal and external customers.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Education and Experience

  • Minimum of 5 years of purchasing experience in a contract manufacturing, electronics manufacturing, PCBA, or similar production environment.
  • Experience purchasing electronic components, mechanical parts, assemblies, equipment, services, or production-related materials preferred.
  • Previous experience working with ERP/MRP systems required.
  • Experience supporting production schedules, material shortages, supplier management, and cost reduction initiatives preferred.

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of purchasing, supply chain, and material planning processes in a manufacturing environment.
  • Working knowledge of contract manufacturing and electronics/PCBA manufacturing preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret material requirements, purchase reports, supplier quotes, and production schedules.
  • Strong negotiation, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal day-to-day direction.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Ability to work under pressure and respond quickly to production and customer needs.
  • Strong communication skills with suppliers, internal teams, and management.
  • Demonstrated ability to build effective supplier and internal customer relationships.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, with strong Excel skills required.
  • Must be able to read, write, and communicate effectively in English.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with electronic component sourcing, lifecycle management, shortages, lead-time challenges, and alternate sourcing.
  • Experience supporting aerospace, medical, defense, or other high-reliability manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with supplier scorecards, cost reduction tracking, and commodity management.
  • Experience working with quality requirements, nonconforming material processes, and supplier corrective actions.

Work Environment

This role operates in a manufacturing and office environment and requires frequent communication with suppliers, internal departments, and production teams. The Senior Buyer must be comfortable managing changing priorities, urgent material needs, supplier escalations, and production-driven deadlines.

Pay Range
$110,000—$125,000 USD

title: Therapy Coordinator
description:
Overview

Step into Leadership - Now offering a $5K Sign-on-Bonus

Why Join Reliant Rehabilitation?

Joining Reliant means becoming part of a team that makes a real difference in the lives of patients and residents across a variety of care communities. As one of the nation’s largest contract therapy providers, Reliant offers unmatched clinical support, professional development, and growth opportunities.

Our leadership team began their careers as therapists, and we take pride in promoting from within. You’ll be supported by a dedicated clinical team that provides ongoing training, proven protocols, and hands-on guidance — ensuring therapy is delivered effectively for patients and in full compliance to support our partners.

With operations in 44 states and more than 900 communities nationwide, Reliant can match your location, schedule, and career goals, wherever your path leads.

What We Offer:

• Competitive compensation packages

• Medical, dental, vision, and company-paid life insurance

• 401(k) with employer match

• PTO Share and Buy-Back Programs

• Maternity and Paternity support program

• Continuing education, mentorship programs and clinical leadership development

• Tuition loan repayment assistance Program

• Flexible scheduling options

Responsibilities

Position Summary:

The Therapy Coordinator (TC) oversees the rehabilitation department to ensure resident needs are met while aligning with company financial goals and adhering to federal and state regulations. This role is responsible for achieving patient care, customer service, and financial objectives through strategic staff scheduling based on patient needs. The Therapy Coordinator maintains professional conduct and fosters positive relationships with clients and facility staff, representing Reliant Rehabilitation’s commitment to quality care and service excellence. All duties are performed in accordance with Reliant Rehabilitation’s policies and procedures.

Key Responsibilities:

• Assign patient scheduling and delegate responsibilities to staff as appropriate

• Coordinate departmental functions with other services to promote teamwork and operational efficiency

• Communicate effectively with facility administration regarding departmental goals, programs, risks, and achievements

• Participate in interdisciplinary meetings including utilization review, quality assurance, resident care conferences, admissions, department head meetings, and community education planning

• Ensure timely and accurate completion of Minimum Data Set (MDS) reporting

• Oversee accurate billing and documentation of services provided

• Maintain a valid state license (as applicable) and stay informed on professional and healthcare industry developments

• Understand and apply relevant billing models and treatment guidelines to deliver clinically appropriate care with measurable outcomes

• Adhere to infection control and environmental safety protocols within the facility

• Attend all required meetings, training, and assignments as directed

• Comply with the responsibilities outlined in the position description for the licensed discipline

• Demonstrate proficiency in reading, writing, speaking, and understanding English for effective communication and documentation

• Maintaining confidentiality as appropriate and ensuring compliance with the state practice act in the state(s) where you are licensed.

Qualifications

Qualifications/Licenses:

• Must hold a degree in Physical Therapy, Physical Therapist Assistant, Occupational Therapy, Occupational Therapy Assistant or Speech-Language Pathology from an accredited institution.

• (2) years of experience as a Physical Therapist, Physical Therapist Assistant, Occupational Therapist, Occupational Therapy Assistant, Speech-Language Pathologist.

title: SAP Data Migration Engineer
description:
Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)

Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary:
We are seeking an experienced SAP Data Migration Engineer to design, execute, and support large-scale data migration initiatives within SAP S/4HANA environments. This role focuses on the full data migration lifecycle — extraction, transformation, validation, reconciliation, and cutover — to ensure accurate, complete, and compliant migration of enterprise data from legacy systems into SAP. The ideal candidate will combine strong hands-on experience with SAP LTMC, SLT, LVM, and S/4HANA migration tools with deep understanding of SAP data structures, business processes, and data governance, and will partner closely with functional teams, business owners, and infrastructure stakeholders during all phases of migration.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Five or more years of SAP data migration experience.
  • Strong hands-on experience with SAP LTMC and S/4HANA migration tools.
  • Experience with SAP SLT replication scenarios.
  • Working knowledge of SAP LVM for system refresh and landscape management.
  • Strong understanding of SAP master and transactional data structures.
  • Experience performing data validation and reconciliation processes.
  • Strong SQL and data analysis skills.
  • Experience working in enterprise SAP landscapes during major implementations.
  • Strong troubleshooting and documentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience participating in S/4HANA greenfield or brownfield implementations.
  • Exposure to SAP Data Services or other ETL platforms.
  • Experience with high-volume, multi-source data migrations.
  • Working knowledge of SAP HANA database structures.
  • SAP S/4HANA certification.

How to Apply

Would you like to know more about this opportunity? For immediate consideration, please send your resume to Harry@bvteck.com or contact us at (908)676-4399. Learn more about Bright Vision Technologies at www.bvteck.com.

title: Transportation Analyst (Journeyman)
description:
At Significance, we believe the best results come from investing in great people. As a woman-owned consulting firm supporting federal civilian and Department of Defense customers, we bring together talented professionals who are passionate about solving complex challenges and making a meaningful impact.

We're proud of the culture we've built - one rooted in trust, collaboration, respect, and genuine relationships. Our people are empowered to share ideas, grow their careers, and deliver exceptional results while supporting missions that matter. It's a culture we're proud of, and one that has earned us recognition as a Washington Business Journal Best Place to Work for seven consecutive years.


Significance, Inc. is seeking a Transportation Analyst (Journeyman) to support the Marine Corps Installation Command (MCICOM) G-4 Transportation Services Branch. This position supports Marine Corps Garrison Mobile Equipment (GME), non-tactical vehicle (NTV), and transportation services programs through transportation policy development, fleet analytics, financial analysis, audit support, task management, and event coordination activities. This position is requires an active Secret position and is a hybrid role onsite in Arlington, VA.

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to independently manage complex tasking, analyze transportation and fleet management data, produce high-quality written products, and operate effectively within Marine Corps task management processes with minimal supervision. This role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, professional communication, and experience supporting DoD transportation, fleet management, or logistics operations.

Required Skills and Experience:

Required Skills and Experience

  • 3–7 years supporting DoD transportation, fleet management, logistics, financial management, or related operations

  • Bachelor's degree

  • Active DoD Secret clearance

  • Experience analyzing transportation, fleet utilization, maintenance, fuel consumption, and lifecycle cost data

  • Experience preparing financial analyses, executive reports, and recommendations

  • Experience researching, drafting, and updating policies, directives, SOPs, or process documentation

  • Experience supporting audit readiness, compliance reviews, or transportation program assessments

Desired Skills:

  • Experience supporting Marine Corps or Navy organizations

  • Familiarity with Fleet Management Information System (FMIS), Fleet Focus, Federal Automotive Statistical Tool (FAST), Program Objective Memorandum (POM) development, or comparable fleet management systems

  • Familiarity with Enterprise Task Management Software Solution (ETMS2) or comparable DoD task management systems

  • Familiarity with Marine Corps transportation policies, including GME, NTV, Class A Vehicles, Domicile-to-Duty, Fleet Manager Award Program, telematics, and related transportation directives

  • Experience coordinating with government stakeholders across multiple organizations

  • Experience planning and coordinating government Working Groups, conferences, workshops, or training events

Candidate Attributes:

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities

  • Strong written communication skills with demonstrated ability to prepare executive-ready reports, briefing materials, and correspondence

  • Ability to rapidly learn and retain new processes and systems

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to deliverable quality

  • Independent execution with minimal direction

  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities while meeting deadlines

  • Ability to identify issues, recommend practical solutions, and proactively communicate risks

  • Ownership mentality and accountability for assigned work products

  • Strong customer service orientation and ability to work collaboratively with government personnel.

At Significance, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location.
We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

title: People & Workplace Project Manager
description:
Overview

At Banner Life Insurance Company, we lead with heart and ambition. Every day, we transform purpose into progress, guided by our unwavering commitment to be better for our customers, clients, and communities, not just today but long-term as well. Our people are the driving force behind everything we achieve. Their passion, purpose, and pursuit of innovation empower us to deliver cutting-edge solutions that support those we serve, ensuring we are here for you, here for good and striving for better.

We’re a forward-thinking company energized by our work and how we show up for one another. Our culture is built on meaningful impact and genuine enjoyment, because we believe great work and great experiences should go hand in hand.

By offering career development opportunities, comprehensive benefits, and programs that support your wellbeing, we help you thrive personally and professionally. We are here for you, here for good and here for better.

The People & Workplace Project Manager will play an important role in helping shape how our people, workplace, and business initiatives come to life. This position is ideal for a proactive project leader who enjoys bringing structure to complex work, partnering across teams, and turning ideas into clear plans and measurable results. In this role, you will lead strategic HR and workplace projects that strengthen how we operate, support organizational priorities, and improve the employee experience. From planning through implementation and follow-up, you will help keep key initiatives moving forward with strong governance, thoughtful stakeholder coordination, clear communication, and a focus on delivering meaningful business impact.

Responsibilities

  • Translate business needs into actionable People & Workplace project plans by developing project charters, defining objectives and success measures, documenting scope, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, priorities, resources, budgets, schedules, and measurable outcomes.
  • Establish and maintain effective project governance, including project schedules, resource plans, RAID logs, dependency management, decision logs, status reporting, stakeholder communications, and steering routines.
  • Coordinate HR leaders, business stakeholders, operational partners and vendors to drive project planning, decisions, issue resolution, readiness, and execution.
  • Identify, manage, and escalate project risks, dependencies, regulatory considerations, scope changes, and operational readiness needs through disciplined risk management and change control practices.
  • Provide clear delivery reporting, recommendations, and decision support to HR leadership, SLT members, and key stakeholders to maintain visibility, accountability, and forward momentum.
  • Support change management, communications, stakeholder engagement, and adoption activities to ensure successful implementation readiness and sustain business impact.
  • Lead or support workplace and operational improvement projects, including facility enhancements, construction-related activities, HR process improvements, systems enhancements, and service delivery improvements.
  • Lead project closeout activities, capture lessons learned, and evaluate outcomes to identify opportunities for continuous improvement, benefits tracking, and stronger delivery across future People & Workplace initiatives.
  • Provide limited operational support to HR initiatives as needed, ensuring primary focus remains on project delivery.

    • Project Types

    • HR systems, process improvement, and service delivery projects
    • Employee experience, engagement, and change initiatives
    • Workplace, facility, and space enhancement projects
    • Compliance-sensitive HR and workplace initiatives
    • Vendor-supported or cross-functional transformation projects

    Success Measures

    • Project plans, risks, dependencies, and decisions are visible, current, and appropriately maintained.
    • Assigned initiatives are delivered within approved scope, timeline, and budget.
    • Stakeholders receive timely, actionable updates that support alignment, decision-making, and accountability.
    • Project launches include readiness, communication, adoption, operational, and support planning.
    • Post-implementation lessons are captured and used to improve future project delivery and benefits tracking.

    Qualifications

    Education

    • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Project Management, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
    • PMP certification required or expected within a defined period
    • CSM preferred
    • Prosci, ACMP or CMI certification preferred

    Experience/Knowledge

    • 5+ years of project management experience leading cross-functional initiatives, preferably within HR, workplace, operations, or business transformation environments.
    • Demonstrated experience leading complex organizational change initiatives
    • Proven experience delivering projects in an agile or hybrid environment
    • Experience coordinating facility-related projects, renovations, construction support, or operational improvements.
    • Experience working with senior leadership, vendors, and cross-functional teams.
    • Working knowledge of business functions, enterprise systems, process improvement initiatives, and process lifecycle development, preferably within HR
    • Understanding of compliance-sensitive business processes and importance of regulatory alignment, preferably within HR
    • Knowledge of facility management practices, including landlord and vendor coordination.

    Skills

    • Strong organization, prioritization, and follow-through skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex projects in a deadline-driven environment.
    • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare project updates, reports, and presentations for leadership.
    • Strong problem-solving and critical thinking skills, with the ability to translate issues, risks, and complex information into actionable recommendations.
    • Detail-oriented and results-driven, with the ability to balance speed, quality, risk, and stakeholder expectations.
    • Adaptable and collaborative, with the ability to work effectively in a rapidly changing, cross-functional environment.

    What’s in it for you?

    The expected hiring compensation range for this position is $109,900 - $151,150 annually. This is a hybrid opportunity working in Frederick, MD

    The total compensation package for this position may include other elements, such as a sign-on bonus, long term incentives, and annual bonuses. This role is eligible to participate in the Annual Incentive Plan. The current target payment for the position is 20% of base salary, modified for corporate and individual performance. Bonuses are pro-rated based on start date. This role has 20 vacation days and 10 sick days that are accrued on a bi-weekly basis. Employees also have 9 paid holidays throughout the calendar year.

    We have a competitive compensation and benefits package focused on your overall wellbeing. Employee benefits include health, life, and dental insurance; 401K with company match up to 6% as well as a pension package; generous time off; and wellbeing initiatives throughout the year (we like doing fun stuff). We’re big on professional development and we’ll support and mentor you in your career progression and expect you to help us pay it forward by helping us develop tomorrow's leaders and growth-focused professionals. We value our teams and our communities and believe in giving back. Enjoy time off to volunteer for those causes that matter most to you!

    If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. The Company reserves the right to change benefits plans at any time.

title: Supervisor Production
description:
Excellence Wanted.

About Us.

Nice-Pak is more than just a Nice Place to Work, and we owe it to our amazing team of nice people to ensure we are hiring new team members who can do more than just meet expectations. We aim to hire excellence.

At Nice-Pak, we manufacture products that touch (literally!) a person's every stage of life - from birth through adulthood into retirement - and worldwide! We are a leading manufacturer of wipes for major grocery, discount, drug, big box, and club membership retailers, and we care deeply about our associates and customers. We care about our environment, too, which is why we stand by our commitment to sustainably source the materials that make our wipes work and support sustainable forestry through education and community engagement.

We live by our purpose of Helping our world stay healthy and well, and it’s important to us that each time we add someone to our Nice-Pak family, we do so with our purpose statement in mind so we can achieve a workforce as special as our customer base.

About the Job.

Why This Job is Important. The Production Supervisor is a leadership position that supports the Production Manager (VSM) and supervises a hard-working team of machine operators who make wipes for our customers. This important position oversees operations on manufacturing value streams to ensure everything runs seamlessly every day so that our customers’ shelves stay full – and so their customers can buy the wipes they need for their baby, teenager, signiﬁcant other or parent (or even their pet!) when they need to. It's a big deal.

Our best Production Supervisors are masters of juggling many things at once and have knowledge of manufacturing basics like quality (cGMP) standards, waste reduction, continuous improvement, and productivity and operational equipment efficiencies (OEE). We also prefer that each supervisor has experience in leading and supervising others. Secondary education in a field related to management or business is also preferred but definitely not required.

We expect our supervisors to be professional, results and performance-oriented, highly engaged in the business, and be able to drive engagement within their teams.

What You Can Expect. As a Production Supervisor, you would be responsible for providing leadership and directing the daily activities of 15 – 30 machine operators on one or more of our manufacturing value streams that produce our wonderful wipes. You also would work closely and partner with cross-functional leaders from the Safety, Quality, Maintenance, and Warehouse departments.

Priorities are keeping employees safe and customers happy. Our Production Supervisors must always “think safe” and anticipate obstacles to prevent downtime on the production lines, meet piece count schedules, and ensure the right products are produced at the right time with the right quality and cost.

Other daily recurring responsibilities include working with spreadsheets, reports, emails, presentations, timekeeping, payroll, and attending or facilitating various meetings. The Production Supervisor communicates to leadership through data using various shift reports to detail the successes and challenges the production team is experiencing. We expect all of our supervisors to anticipate challenges and solve problems creatively.

This is What You Can Count on From Us:

  • We will provide a safe work environment.
  • Working conditions free from unusual hazards or otherwise signiﬁcantly unpleasant conditions – our production areas are comfortably climate-controlled and have the same temperature year-round! It smells amazing on the production ﬂoor, and there is a chance you could go home smelling better than you did when you arrived at work.
  • We want you to succeed and will invest in you and your career
  • You can count on us to encourage diversity, equity, and an atmosphere of inclusion.
  • Great benefits including 401(k) match, vision, medical and dental coverage. We also offer tuition reimbursement among other benefits.
  • Excellent pay, based on experience. The range for this position in the Indiana market is $70–80k with additional bonus opportunities.

The Non-Negotiable Things.

  • No shortcuts are allowed. We expect you to support our culture of safety and hold others accountable to it, even if it is uncomfortable.
  • The Nice-Pak adheres to all local, state, and federal laws, and we expect every leader to do so as well.
  • You will work with and lead many people, so you must be able to communicate in a respectful, professional, and purposeful way, both in writing and verbally.
  • You must be able to read and understand basic math principles, solve problems, and be resourceful on a computer, including Microsoft Office.
  • You must commit to taking care of your This means approving payroll on time, coaching for success, being a good listener, providing direct feedback in a respectful manner, and being fair.

The Important HR and Legal Stuff

Nice-Pak is an equal-opportunity employer. We hire the most qualiﬁed people to join our team and do not tolerate discriminant behavior. We also adhere to ADA standards and review any reasonable accommodations to try to help you do your job in the best way for you when requested. We also conduct various pre-employment screenings, including drug tests as allowed by law.

title: Conformal Coating Operator
description:
Conformal Coating Operator

Position Summary

The Conformal Coating Operator is responsible for operating, monitoring, and supporting automated and semi-automated conformal coating equipment to apply protective coatings to printed circuit boards (PCBs). This role ensures boards are coated accurately, consistently, and in accordance with workmanship standards, customer requirements, and internal procedures. The operator works closely with technicians, leads, and quality personnel to maintain throughput, quality, and process stability.

Key Responsibilities

Machine Operation & Production

  • Set up, operate, and monitor conformal coating equipment (selective spray, automated systems, or manual-assisted processes).

  • Load and unload PCBAs, ensuring correct orientation, fixturing, and program selection.

  • Start, stop, and adjust machine parameters as directed by work instructions or process documentation.

  • Monitor coating application for proper coverage, thickness, and alignment during production runs.

Process Monitoring & Quality

  • Perform in-process inspections using UV light, magnification, or inspection lamps to verify coating quality.

  • Identify coating defects such as skips, bubbles, bridging, overspray, or masking issues.

  • Escalate quality concerns or recurring defects to leads, supervisors, or process engineering.

  • Support minor touch-up or corrective actions as trained and approved.

Masking & Board Preparation

  • Apply and remove masking materials per work instructions prior to and after coating.

  • Prepare boards for coating by verifying cleanliness, masking integrity, and traveler accuracy.

  • Assist with demasking and post-coating handling to prevent damage to coated assemblies.

Equipment & Material Handling

  • Refill coating materials, solvents, and consumables following safety and handling procedures.

  • Perform routine machine cleaning and basic preventive maintenance tasks.

  • Maintain coating equipment, fixtures, and workstations in a clean and organized condition.

  • Properly label, store, and handle chemicals in accordance with safety and environmental requirements.

Documentation & Reporting

  • Accurately complete travelers, production logs, and inspection checklists.

  • Record lot information, machine settings (as required), and any process deviations.

  • Communicate production status, downtime, or issues during shift handoffs.

Compliance & Safety

  • Follow all manufacturing instructions, IPC workmanship standards, and ESD control procedures.

  • Adhere to chemical safety, PPE, and environmental regulations.

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and compliant work area at all times.

Qualifications

Preferred

  • Experience operating manufacturing or automated equipment in an electronics or PCBA environment.

  • Familiarity with conformal coating processes and materials (acrylic, silicone, urethane).

  • Ability to read and follow work instructions, travelers, and process documentation.

  • Basic understanding of IPC-A-610 standards or willingness to obtain certification.

  • Comfortable working with UV inspection tools and precision equipment.

Soft Skills

  • Strong attention to detail and process discipline.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a production team.

  • Clear communication skills and willingness to escalate issues.

  • Dependable, safety-conscious, and quality-focused.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand or sit for extended periods.

  • Fine-motor coordination for handling PCBAs and masking materials.

  • Ability to lift up to 20 lbs as required.

Benefits

  • 401(k) with company match

  • Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance

  • Paid time off and company holidays

  • Opportunities for advancement in a growing, high-tech manufacturing environment

Schedule

  • 8-hour shift, Monday–Friday

  • Overtime and weekend availability as needed

Pay Range
$20—$24 USD

Core Responsibilities: What You'll Own

Technical Field Leadership

  • Serve as the primary on-site technical authority, translating design specifications into field execution while maintaining rigorous quality and safety standards. Make real-time engineering decisions that balance performance, cost, and schedule.
  • Site Investigation & Geotechnical Analysis
  • Conduct slope assessments, geotechnical testing, and rope-access inspections in challenging terrain. Develop rapid-turnaround site characterizations that inform design decisions and mitigation strategy.
  • Design Implementation & Adaptive Problem-Solving
  • Implement complex geohazard mitigation systems (soil stabilization, rockfall prevention, slope reinforcement). When field conditions diverge from design assumptions, develop and validate alternative solutions in real time—with engineering rigor.

Coordination & Documentation

  • Coordinate directly with project management, engineering staff, and construction teams. Document as-built conditions, material performance, and construction progress with precision for technical reporting and project controls. Be the reliable source of truth on field conditions.

Safety & Quality Ownership

  • Maintain and champion safety protocols in the field. Identify hazards, propose controls, and ensure every team member goes home safe. Quality is non-negotiable—develop the discipline and systems to prevent defects.

Who Succeeds Here: Good vs. Great

A Good Field Engineer follows specifications, documents observations, and reports issues up the chain.

A Great Field Engineer owns outcomes. They possess the intellectual horsepower to understand why design decisions were made, anticipate failure modes before they occur, and develop creative solutions under constraints. They communicate with precision, take initiative without waiting for direction, and build trust through reliability and sound judgment. They view field data not as check-box documentation but as evidence that informs continuous improvement.

You should apply if you:

  • Hold a Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, or related field (EIT or PE certification valued; exceptional candidates without formal credentials will be considered based on demonstrated capability).
  • Have a track record of translating technical knowledge into measurable outcomes—examples: identified cost savings, improved safety metrics, accelerated project timelines, or delivered solutions under difficult field constraints.
  • Are analytically rigorous and comfortable with ambiguity. You can assess incomplete information, develop hypotheses, test them, and iterate toward solutions.
  • Communicate with precision—both in writing (reports, emails, technical documentation) and verbally. Clarity is a proxy for clear thinking.
  • Demonstrate extreme ownership: you don't blame systems or others; you ask "What could I have done differently?" and act on it.
  • Are energized by high-responsibility field work and willing to spend 70% of your time traveling to active project sites across the U.S., Canada, or Australasia.
  • Are technically fluent in Microsoft Office, AutoCAD, and slope stability software (SLIDE, PLAXIS, or equivalent). If you haven't used a specific tool, you learn it quickly.
